AuthorityRef.description:
Authoritative scope of a source binding. A mutable path, label, or host
profile cannot be represented as authority.

CancellationStage.description: Exact stage at which cancellation or deadline state was observed.

CanonicalGitRefNameV1.description: A validated full native Git ref name, such as `refs/heads/main`.

CanonicalGitRefPrefix.description:
A validated ref/branch prefix. Branch naming accepts a short branch prefix
(for example `tracedecay/`) while protected-ref selectors use full
`refs/.../` prefixes.

required_source.description: The seam that must be closed to feed this route with live data.

CodeIndexWorktreeFreshnessV1.description:
Freshness/generation state for one mounted worktree. Unpopulated until the
scheduler-registry read port is wired into the dashboard state.

hook_hint_count.description: Pending hook-hint count, when cheaply available.

last_reconcile_micros.description: Last reconcile observation time (microseconds since the Unix epoch).

latest_generation_id.description: Latest sealed generation identity, when a complete generation exists.

worktree_root.description: Display path of the mounted worktree root.

DashboardAuthorizationV1.description:
Authorization outcome for the read. On the loopback single-user dashboard a
legal local read is [`Self::Authorized`]; the other variants are retained so
the contract can express `unauthorized` (identity absent/expired), `denied`
(known identity lacks permission), and `redacted` reads without a schema
change.

DashboardCoverageCompletenessV1.description:
Coverage completeness axis. `Unsupported` distinguishes "the source that
would establish coverage is not wired" from `Unknown` ("coverage could not
be determined").

DashboardCoverageV1.description:
Coverage statement. Counts are optional; an unknown denominator is `None`,
never a fabricated `0`/`100%`. The completeness axis is authoritative — the
frontend never derives `complete` from a `matched == eligible` coincidence.

denominator.description:
Denominator for a percentage. `None` means the denominator is unknown, so
the frontend must not render a meter or a percentage.

DashboardDomainStateV1.description:
The normative dashboard domain-state union.

The first sixteen variants are the plan's exact `DashboardDomainState`
discriminated union. [`Self::Unsupported`] is the PR14 backend-gap binding
state: the read model's HTTP surface exists, but its live producer/source is
not yet wired server-side. It is never healthy or empty — the frontend
renders a distinct "not yet available" state — and it is deliberately
separate from [`Self::UnsupportedSchema`] (an undecodable schema/variant).

oneOf.description:
The read model exists but its live producer/source is not yet wired
server-side (plan §"Known backend gaps"). Distinct from every "healthy"
or "empty" state.

DashboardEnvelopeV1.description:
The normative read-model envelope. Every V2 read-model route returns exactly
this shape; only `payload` varies by route.

DashboardFreshnessStateV1.description:
Freshness of the observed state relative to its live source watermark.
`Absent` (no source produced anything) and `Unsupported` (no source wired)
are distinct from `Stale` (behind the watermark) and `Unknown`.

DashboardFreshnessV1.description:
Freshness statement plus the optional observation stamp/watermark it was
judged against.

DashboardLegalActionKindV1.description:
The legal-action reference kinds a read model may attach. This mirrors the
plan's action vocabulary reduced to the read surface: the dashboard only
renders these references and submits them through the owning application
operation; it never constructs an effect inline.

DashboardLegalActionRefV1.description:
A reference to one owner-supplied legal action. `operation` names the owning
application operation; the dashboard never embeds argv, a path, or an inline
effect.

DashboardScopeV1.description:
Exact scope the envelope was resolved for. A deep link/query never falls
back to a title, path, or latest version to recover scope.

project_id.description: Registered project id, when the store is profile-backed.

store_root.description: Resolved active project store root (display path).

DashboardTimeV1.description:
Valid time and observation time, kept separate. `observation_time` is when
the daemon observed the state; `valid_time` is when the state was true in the
modelled domain (absent when a read model has no distinct valid time).

observation_time_micros.description: Observation time in microseconds since the Unix epoch. Always present.

valid_time_micros.description: Domain valid time in microseconds since the Unix epoch, when distinct.

DashboardVersionV1.description:
Entity and graph version identities pinned by the envelope. Both are
optional: a read model with no versioned graph state leaves them absent
rather than inventing `0`/`latest`.

DashboardWatermarkV1.description:
Opaque monotone source watermark. The frontend compares watermarks for
staleness but never parses their internal structure.

source.description: Which source the watermark belongs to.

Deadline.description: One immutable deadline supplied by the caller or upstream admission layer.

DoctorConfirmationRequirementV1.description:
Whether an owning operation requires an explicit human confirmation before it
may perform its admitted mutating effect.

oneOf.description: An explicit confirmation is required before the action may run.
No confirmation is required (still dispatched through the owner).

DoctorCoverageCompletenessV1.description: Whether Doctor observed all of a family's evidence sources.

oneOf.description: Every relevant evidence source for the family was observed.
Some evidence sources were observed; others were omitted.
Whether coverage is complete could not be determined.

DoctorCoverageStatementV1.description: A bounded, human-readable coverage statement plus its completeness.

DoctorEvidenceRefV1.description:
A typed reference to one piece of evidence Doctor composed into a finding.

The `family` records which audited input surface produced the evidence, so
a finding may cross-cite evidence from more than one family without losing
provenance.

DoctorEvidenceReferenceV1.description:
Durable, non-disclosing reference to one owning-authority evidence
record (for example a `FeedbackFindingId`, configuration revision, or
runtime read coverage anchor). Doctor stores the reference only; the
owning authority remains the single source of the record.

DoctorEvidenceStateV1.description:
Exact Doctor evidence states from Plan 09 §PR14.

Missing, partial, or unknown truth never becomes healthy or clean. Only
[`DoctorEvidenceStateV1::HealthyCompleteCoverage`] asserts a healthy result,
and only when its finding carries complete coverage (see
[`DoctorFindingV1::new`]).

oneOf.description: The owning authority does not support this evidence on this platform.
The evidence source is supported but produced nothing.
The evidence exists but is behind the current generation/watermark.
The evidence proves a degraded but observed condition.
Only part of the evidence was observed.
The evidence state could not be determined.
Authorization to read the evidence was denied.
The evidence proves a healthy condition with complete coverage.

DoctorFamilyConsultationV1.description: Whether a family was consulted from an observed source or is unavailable.

oneOf.description: A source produced observed evidence for this family.
No observed evidence; the family is carried as unavailable.

DoctorFamilyCoverageV1.description: The consultation status of one finding family within a report.

DoctorFamilyUnavailableReasonV1.description: Why a finding family could not be consulted from an observed source.

oneOf.description: No source port is wired for this family in this composition.
The source is unsupported on this build/platform.
The source is supported but produced nothing.
The source read was denied.
The source state could not be determined.

DoctorFindingFamilyV1.description:
Stable Doctor finding families.

The initial list is derived from Plan 14's observable classes (advisory
findings from Brain/Explorer/Loom/Code/Observatory) and the legacy
`core_doctor` checks (graph quick-check, temporal/migration health,
configuration compatibility drift, semantic runtime, session ingest).
Each family maps to one audited typed input surface. The set is kept small
and honest; new families are added through a future versioned enum rather
than by widening the meaning of an existing variant.

oneOf.description:
PR13 advisory/scout findings (GitHub review, CI localization,
proximity, context scout) — `crate::advisory` / domain feedback.

Desired-versus-effective configuration and compatibility drift
(Plan 20 `ProjectConfigurationRuntime` / `ConfigurationControlPlane`).

Store, graph, and temporal runtime health plus migration coverage
(`RuntimeReadOperationV1` health family, `StoreRuntimeHandle`).

Storage retention, size, and efficiency over Plan 26 observability read
models (Plan 38 §7). Distinct from [`Self::StorageRuntime`] health: this
family surfaces over-budget stores, identity-drift orphans, stale branch
DBs, quarantined incident debris, and retention backlog. The typed
subclass vocabulary is [`DoctorStorageFindingKindV1`].

Language-server / analyzer engine status (Plan 35 LSP gateway,
`AnalyzerState`).
Semantic search / index runtime state (indexing, stale, unavailable).

Denominator-safe measurement and telemetry health (Plan 26 analytics /
accounting read models, session ingest).

DoctorFindingV1.description:
One canonical Doctor finding.

A finding pins its diagnosis `family`, its evidence `state`, the typed
evidence it composed, a coverage statement, and an optional reference to an
owner-supplied remediation. Construction enforces the Plan 09 §PR14
invariants that keep unknown/partial evidence from collapsing into a healthy
or clean result.

DoctorFindingsPayloadV1.description:
The canonical Doctor report projection. `entries` retains the storage
subclass attached by the kernel; remediation descriptors are emitted only
after the kernel registry resolves the finding's owner-supplied reference.

kind_statuses.description:
Storage-route-only producer-source coverage. General Doctor responses
omit this additive field; `/api/storage/findings` always supplies all
five Plan 38 producer statuses.

DoctorOwningOperationRefV1.description:
Reference to the owning application operation that would perform a
remediation (its capability or use-case identity). Doctor names the
operation; it never embeds argv, a path, or an inline effect.

DoctorOwningSurfaceV1.description:
The application surface that owns dispatch of a remediation operation.

The kernel names the owner so a transport can route confirmation and dispatch
to the correct surface; it never dispatches itself.

oneOf.description: The configuration control plane (Plan 20).
The storage retention/lifecycle runtime (Plan 38).
The daemon/runtime supervisor.
The host/agent integration installer/repairer (Plan 27).
The semantic/code index runtime (Plan 35 / semantic index).
The canonical advisory feedback read owner (PR11–PR13).

DoctorRemediationDescriptorV1.description:
A typed description of what an owner-supplied remediation operation would do.

This is a *description*, not an effect. It never carries argv, a path, or an
inline action, and resolving it performs no work.

DoctorRemediationKindV1.description:
Preview-versus-action distinction for an owner-supplied remediation.

Doctor never repairs; it references an owning application operation. A
preview pins expected state without mutating; an action is the owning
operation's admitted effect. Both are invoked through the owning operation,
never inline.

oneOf.description: A non-mutating preview owned by the responsible operation.
An admitted mutating action owned by the responsible operation.

DoctorRemediationRefV1.description:
A reference to an owner-supplied remediation.

Doctor never repairs directly; it names the owning application operation
and whether a preview or action is offered. The caller invokes that owning
operation through its normal admitted path.

DoctorReportCoverageV1.description:
The report-wide coverage statement: which families were consulted versus
unavailable, plus an overall completeness and a bounded human statement.

DoctorReportEntryV1.description:
One entry in a Doctor report: a canonical finding plus, for the storage
family, its typed subclass. The subclass is present only for storage findings
(a non-storage entry never carries one).

DoctorStorageFindingKindV1.description:
Typed subclasses of the [`DoctorFindingFamilyV1::Storage`] finding family
(Plan 38 §7).

The storage family never reports a silent overage: each subclass names one
observable retention/size condition Doctor surfaces over the Plan 26 size
observability read models. The set is closed and grows only through a future
versioned enum, never by widening an existing subclass.

oneOf.description: A store exceeds its owner-configured soft size budget.

A store whose project identity no longer resolves to a live repository
root (identity-drift orphan), reported with age and size.

Branch-scoped databases whose git refs are gone and are awaiting
lifecycle removal.

Quarantined recovery/corruption artifacts are present and awaiting
collection.

Retention-eligible rows or stores are past their window and awaiting
offload/collection.

EffectClass.description:
The stable effect classification of one application operation.

Git index writes remain separate classes so policy cannot accidentally
substitute one index mutation for another.

EffectReceipt.description:
Durable effect proof. It records identities and receipts, never credentials
or arbitrary command text.

HostKindV1.description:
Canonical stock host surfaces shared by catalog, packaging, delivery, and
conformance consumers. A host surface is not itself evidence that the PR6
observation-capture capability is fixture-backed.

OperationBudgetUsage.description: Bounded work accounting supplied by an owning port or transaction.

OperationId.description:
Stable operation identity. The originating authorized request owns the
identity; paths, labels, and client-selected payloads never participate.

OperationReceipt.description:
Canonical operation evidence. An admitted failure remains represented here
rather than being replaced by a transport exception.

OperationTermination.description: Terminal state after an operation has been admitted.

ProtectedChange.description:
The protected configuration operation set. Ordinary scalar mutations are
intentionally absent; they activate directly after validation.

ResolvedScope.description:
The resolved PR11 scope is one exact project/repository/worktree root.

Paths, CWDs, labels, and mutable branch spellings are deliberately absent.

ScopeAccessRule.description:
Restrictive policy input. An allow never grants capabilities absent from
the independently authorized capability set passed to the resolver.

ScopeAccessSubjectV1.description:
Typed rule selectors. Unset dimensions match all values at that dimension,
but at least one dimension must be constrained. Free-form paths, labels,
collection names, and branch names are deliberately absent.

ScopeSourceBinding.description:
A source-to-authority binding. It stores only the source kind, a redacted
locator digest, and the pre-resolved authority reference.

SensitiveFilesystemLocatorV1.description:
Reference-only filesystem locator. The raw path is sealed outside this
contract; only the privacy-bound locator digest and sealed-value digest are
representable here.

StorageByteSizeV1.description:
A byte size measurement. A newtype keeps sizes from being confused with
counts, ratios, or timestamps in the read models and producers.

StorageFindingKindStatusV1.description: Source-coverage status for one typed storage finding producer.

StorageFindingSourceStateV1.description:
Whether one Plan 38 producer had enough source evidence to report a real
result. This is source coverage, not a health grade: `Real` can describe a
clean observation or a problem finding.

StorageTelemetryPayloadV1.description:
Telemetry payload: one entry per distinct store the dashboard holds a
connection to.

budget_note.description: Where budgets come from, stated once for the whole read.

growth_note.description: The growth window's coverage, stated once for the whole read.

StorageTelemetryReadV1.description:
The typed result of one telemetry read attempt.

The port is *total*: it never fails silently into a healthy or empty result.
A platform that cannot query `dbstat`/pragmas reports [`Self::Unsupported`];
a denied read reports [`Self::Denied`]; an undetermined read reports
[`Self::Unknown`]. Each maps to a distinct, honest Doctor evidence state.

oneOf.description: A size sample was observed.
The runtime cannot expose page-count telemetry on this build/platform.
Authorization to read the store's telemetry was denied.
The telemetry state could not be determined.

StoreBudgetDimensionV1.description: The budget-evaluation dimension, sourced from owner configuration.

oneOf.description: An owner-configured soft budget was evaluated against the live sample.

setting_key.description: The owner setting this budget came from.

oneOf.description:
The budget source is wired and readable, but this owner configured no
budget for this store. A missing *setting*, not a missing *feature*.

setting_key.description: The setting an owner would set to configure a budget here.

oneOf.description:
The budget could not be determined: the resolved configuration was
unreadable, or no size sample was observed to evaluate against.

StoreBudgetEvaluationV1.description: The outcome of evaluating a store size against its soft budget.

StoreGrowthDimensionV1.description:
The per-store growth dimension. Growth is only ever reported over the window
the server actually observed, and that window is named in `coverage`.

oneOf.description:
The first watermark of this daemon lifetime: a real measurement with no
earlier point to compare against. Not "zero growth".
Growth observed across at least two watermarks in the window.

growth_bytes.description:
Signed delta over the window; a shrinking store reports a negative
number rather than saturating to zero.

oneOf.description: No watermark could be recorded because the size read failed.

StoreKeyV1.description:
Logical name of one owner-profile store (for example `sessions.db`,
`graph.db`, or `branches/feature-x`). Never an absolute on-disk path.

StoreSizeSampleV1.description:
One cheap size sample for a single store, derived from page-count pragmas.

`total_bytes` is `page_count * page_size`; `free_bytes` is
`freelist_pages * page_size`. Both are recorded so the free-page ratio and
the reclaimable-bytes estimate (Plan 38 §6 compaction) can be computed
without re-reading the store.

measured_at.description: Wall-clock microseconds at which the size was measured.

StoreTelemetryEntryV1.description:
One store's telemetry entry. One entry per distinct store **file**, not per
dashboard role.

path.description: Display path of the store file.

read.description:
The typed telemetry read: `observed` with a sample, or `unknown` when the
pragma read failed. Never silently healthy.

role.description:
The dashboard's primary role label for the store (`graph` / `memory` /
`lcm` / `savings`). Retained for compatibility; see `roles` for the
complete set.

roles.description:
Every dashboard role served by this one store file. More than one role
here means the roles share a database, not that a store was duplicated.

store.description:
Stable store key (the store's file name), or the raw file name when it is
not a valid [`StoreKeyV1`].

UtcMicros.description: UTC timestamp represented as microseconds from the Unix epoch.

WorkTopologyPolicyV1.description:
Complete V1 policy. Partial values are intentionally impossible: callers
must provide the entire policy and validation rejects adapter-local defaults.
